Arguments 9-10 are on the stack. Returns the advanced display-list pointer. Side effects: display-list output. Callers: 1 (world_draw_character_model_cb).

column2: void world_build_character_quad(int part, float *verts, int direction, int move_state, int frame)
column3: Fills 4 vertices of 6 words {u, v, colour, x, y, z} for one part of a generic character sprite: the direction pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) selects a group 0-3 and the cell {u, v} is read from 0x090f8984 (move state 0, idle) or 0x090f898c (move state 1, walking) + frame * 8 + group * 0x38 (other move-state values are used as a pointer); the cell is 0x33 pixels wide in a 512 x 256 texture; part 1 takes rows v..v+0x3d (upper), part 0 rows v+0x3d..v+0x54 (lower); x from -0.3984375 to the constant 0x090f8c14, y between the constants 0x090f8c04-0x090f8c10; colour 0xffffffff, z = 0. Side effects: writes verts[0..23]. Callers: 1 (world_draw_character_sprite).

column2: void world_build_character_part_quad(int part, float *verts, int direction, int cell_id, int move_state, int frame)
column3: Fills 4 screen-space vertices for one part of a model-entry character: gets the sprite cells (world_get_character_sprite_cell), projects the object origin and a point 1.25 units above it through projection * view * model (GU matrices 0-2 read back, scaled by 64), and builds a 51-pixel-wide quad (x - 25 .. x + 26) in a 512 x 256 texture: part 0 uses the cell picked by cell_id, 50 rows high, placed 80 - 12 pixels above the projected origin plus the per-frame vertical offset; part 1 uses the cell from the animation table, 64 rows high, from the origin to 64 - 12 pixels above it; depth values interpolated between the two projected points; colour 0xffffffff; u is mirrored when the cell lookup reports a flipped direction. Side effects: writes verts[0..23]. Callers: 1 (world_draw_character_sprite_parts).

column2: void world_get_character_sprite_cell(int *out_u, int *out_v, int *out_offset, int *out_u2, int *out_v2, int *out_flip, int direction, int cell_id, int move_state, int frame)
column3: Maps a direction 0-7 to a sprite column and mirror flag (0 -> column 2, 1 -> 0, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 1, 4 -> 4, 5 -> 1 mirrored, 6 -> 3 mirrored, 7 -> 0 mirrored) and returns: *out_u = column * 0x33 + 0xff when cell_id % 10 >= 5, *out_v = (cell_id % 10 % 5) * 0x32 (the cell chosen by the character's model id); *out_u2/*out_v2 = the {u, v} pair of the animation table 0x090f8a64 (idle) or 0x090f8a6c (walking) + frame * 8 + column * 0x38; *out_offset (when non-NULL) = the signed byte of 0x090f8b80 + column * 7 + frame (+1 when walking), or direction for other move states; *out_flip (when non-NULL) = mirror flag. Arguments 9-10 are on the stack. Side effects: writes the outputs. Callers: 1 (world_build_character_part_quad).

Pushes the three GU matrices and loads screen-space ones: projection = orthographic (-240, 240, -136, 136, -10000, 10000), view and model identity; leaves matrix mode 2. Side effects: the GU matrix stacks. Callers: 1 (world_draw_character_sprite_parts).
Pops the model, view and projection matrices pushed by world_push_screen_matrices and leaves matrix mode 2. Side effects: the GU matrix stacks. Callers: 1 (world_draw_character_sprite_parts).

Opens the stencil-shadow pass of the free-roam field: clears the stencil buffer to 0 (system_ge_write_clear with flags 2), disables texturing (GE state 9), disables depth writes (depth mask 1), enables the stencil test (state 3) with function ALWAYS (1), ref 0, mask 0xff, enables face culling (state 5) and masks all colour writes (pixel mask 0xffffff). Side effects: GE commands in list. Callers: 1 (world_draw_object_list).

Draws one shadow volume into the stencil buffer (z-pass method): builds the model matrix translate(position) x translate(const 0x090fc1e0) x shadow basis (0x09105ac0, field_3d_set_shadow_basis) x scale(const) x translate(const) x scale(const) x scale(radius, k, radius); draws the volume mesh (a 0x30-vertex strip at 0x090fc200 and a 0x48-vertex triangle list at 0x090fc5c0, vertex type 0x143) twice: with stencil operation INCR (4) on depth pass and front face 1, then DECR (5) with front face 0. Returns the advanced display list. Side effects: GE commands, the GUM matrix stack (pushed and popped). Callers: 1 (world_draw_object_list).

Closes the stencil-shadow pass: restores texturing, front face, depth writes and colour writes, then with the stencil test enabled (function LESS (4), ref 0, i.e. stencil > 0), texturing and depth test disabled, draws a full-screen 480 x 272 sprite in colour 0x80000000 with alpha blending (half-transparent black over every shadowed pixel); then disables the stencil test, re-enables texturing and the depth test and sets the colour to opaque white. Side effects: GE commands in list. Callers: 1 (world_draw_object_list).

Read from the disassembly: chains three set-up calls through the display-list pointer they return: field_3d_setup_field_render_state(), field_3d_set_field_camera(list), world_apply_light_colour(list). Callers: 3 (world_draw_object_list, world_draw_map, world_sandwich_roulette_draw_golden_egg).

Writes the base render state of the free-roam field into list: screen offset (0x710, 0x778), viewport centre (0x800, 0x800) 480 x 272, depth range 0xffff..0, blend function add/src-alpha/one-minus-src-alpha with blending off, scissor 480 x 272 enabled, alpha function GREATER ref 0 with the alpha test off, depth function GEQUAL with the depth test on, front face 1 and culling on, texturing off, smooth shading, clip planes on, colour 0xff0000ff, fog 50..100 in colour 0x404040 with fog off; loads an orthographic projection (system_gum_ortho(-240, 240, -136, 136, -10000, 10000)) multiplied by the scale vector 0x090fcb80, identity view and model matrices, clear colour/depth/stencil 0 and linear texture filtering. The return value is the advanced display list (the decompiler shows void; field_3d_begin_field_scene passes the result on). Side effects: GE commands, GUM matrices. Callers: 2 (field_3d_apply_field_scene_state, field_3d_begin_field_scene).

Sets the free-roam field view matrix: target = the player position (world_get_player_position), eye = target + the offset 0x090f3e30/34/38, up = the constant 0x090fcb90; while the shake flag 0x09106710 is set, adds the shake vector 0x09106730 to eye and target; calls field_3d_camera_set_look_at, marks the matrices dirty, copies the camera's position (+0x30 of field_3d_get_camera) to 0x09106740 and resets the model matrix. Read from the disassembly (the decompiler loses the stores): builds a 32-bit hide mask in which bit i is set unless group i belongs to the variant: variant 1 keeps groups 5-9 visible, variant 2 groups 10-14, any other value groups 0-4 (all other bits set); then tail-jumps to field_3d_set_group_mask(inst, mask) through its import stub. So each map mesh carries up to three 5-group variants and the light period (world_get_map_variant_for_period) picks one. No return value. Side effects: writes the model instance's group mask (+0x64). Callers: 1 (world_bind_map_archive, once per map mesh).

column2: int field_3d_map_stencil_draw_callback(void **list_ref, void *model, int mesh, int material, int phase)
column3: Per-material draw callback of the free-roam map that turns a mesh into a stencil writer (phase is the fifth argument, in register t0): phase 0 (before drawing) masks colour writes (pixel mask 0xffffff) and depth writes, enables the depth and stencil tests with function ALWAYS ref 1 and operation REPLACE on depth pass, so the mesh writes stencil 1 where it is visible; phase 1 (after) restores colour and depth writes. Writes the advanced display list back to *list_ref. model, mesh and material are not used. Returns 0. Side effects: GE commands. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer: the map model's draw callback).

column2: int field_3d_map_material_dd_callback(void **list_ref, void *model, int mesh, int material, int phase)
column3: Per-material draw callback of the free-roam map: reads the material name pointer at *(model +0xc) + mesh x 0xa4 + material x 0x20 + 0x1c and flags the material when the name is longer than 6 characters and contains one of four substrings (0x090fd16c, 0x090fd174, 0x090fd17c, 0x090fd184). For a flagged material it enables a GE state before drawing (phase 1) and disables it after (phase 0); which state is hidden by the decompiler (open question). Writes the list back to *list_ref. Returns 0. Side effects: GE commands. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer: the map model's draw callback).

Opens the stencil pass of the free-roam map (same commands as field_3d_begin_shadow_stencil): clears the stencil to 0, disables texturing, disables depth writes, enables the stencil test with function ALWAYS ref 0 mask 0xff, enables culling and masks colour writes. Side effects: GE commands in list. Callers: 1 (world_draw_map).

Draws a stencil volume at position for the free-roam map (z-pass inc/dec like field_3d_draw_shadow_volume): matrix translate(position) x translate(const 0x090fd1c0) x (rotate Y by a constant on map 3) x a Y/Z-flip matrix x scale(0x090fd1b0) x translate(0x090fd190) x scale(0x090fd1a0); on map 3 the scale is (1.75, k, const 0x090f80c0); on maps 0xd-0x14 and 0x26, when position x / 0.5 is 12 and z / 0.5 is 5, the z scale is reduced by 0x090f80c4 (world_get_current_map). Draws the mesh (a 15-vertex strip at 0x090fd1d0 and 6 triangles' vertices at 0x090fd248, vertex type 0xa1) with stencil operation INCR and front face 1, then DECR and front face 0. Returns the advanced list. Side effects: GE commands, the GUM matrix stack (pushed and popped). Callers: 1 (world_draw_map).

Closes the map stencil pass with a pulsing tint: pulse = |frame % 40 - 20| / 20 from the frame counter (word 0 of system_get_frame_timing); restores texturing, front face, depth and colour writes, then with the stencil test LESS ref 0 (stencil > 0), texturing and depth test off, draws a full-screen 480 x 272 sprite in colour 0x8080ff with alpha 32 + 32 x pulse and alpha blending; finally disables the stencil test, re-enables texturing and the depth test and sets the colour to opaque white. Side effects: GE commands in list. Callers: 1 (world_draw_map).

column2: void ui_pda_open(void *heap, void *archive, int mode, int restricted)
column3: Opens the PDA: allocates its 0x2a0-byte block from heap on first use (pointer 0x09899de8) and clears it; stores heap (+0xa8), archive (+0xac), restricted (+0x298: main menu limited to 5 entries), the flag 0x09899dec (+0x29c: shows submenu entry 1) and the partner record words 0x09899df0-0x09899df8 (+0x288-+0x290); finds pda_pack01.gim (+0xb0), the cover model, event_name.bin and the option strings in archive; resets the cover animation; mode (+0x294): 0 slides the PDA in from x = -335 (state 1, sound 0x7a58), 1 opens the three-entry submenu (state 9), 2 the five-entry submenu (state 0xb, main cursor 1), 3 the main menu (state 3), 4 the status screen (state 4), 5 the options (state 0xc), 6 the main menu with cursor 6; the non-zero modes start already in place (x = the home x at +8, cover animation at its end). Side effects: heap, PDA block, sound. Callers: 4 (world_field_req_begin_walk, world_field_read_command_input, world_field_command_step, world_open_event_command_bar).

Per-frame step of the PDA state machine (state s16 +0 of the block 0x09899de8). An open confirmation prompt (byte +0x166 = 4 or 5, list window +0x168) is polled first: yes (button 2) returns 0xd (prompt 4) or 0xb (prompt 5), busy returns 0, otherwise the prompt is closed (0xff). States: 1 slides in (x = (home - 0x14f) * (10 - n)^2 / 100 over 10 frames, then state 2, sound 0x7a59); 2 reveals the main menu over 0xe steps (+0xb8) then state 3; 3 main menu input (ui_pda_step_main_menu); 4 status screen: circle or cross (0x6000) plays 0x7a06 and returns to state 2 (or closes, state 0x10, when opened in mode 4); 8 reveals the three-entry menu (6 steps) then 9; 9 returns ui_pda_step_three_entry_menu(); 10 reveals the five-entry menu then 0xb; 0xb returns ui_pda_step_five_entry_menu(); 0xc opens the options (ui_options_open(heap, archive, 2)) and goes to 0xd; 0xd steps them and on result 2 frees them and returns to state 2 (or closes when opened in mode 5); 0xe returns 0xc; 0xf slides out and then closes; 0x10 closes the PDA (ui_pda_close) and returns 1. Returns 0 while running, 1 when closed (or no PDA), or a command code (3-5, 6-10, 0xb, 0xc, 0xd). Side effects: PDA block, sounds, options. Callers: 1 (world_field_command_step).

Draws the PDA when open: font shadow and colour codes on, Japanese line-break flag (language 0) or space trimming; into GE layer 3 with texturing and alpha blending the screen (ui_pda_draw_screen) and its frame (ui_pda_draw_screen_frame) at the PDA position (s16 +4/+6); then the 3D cover (ui_pda_setup_3d_view, ui_pda_draw_cover_model); then into GE layer 4 the screen fade (system_draw_fade) and the confirmation prompt list window (+0x168) unless the prompt byte +0x166 is 0xff. Side effects: GE layers 3 and 4, font state. Callers: 1 (world_draw_field_ui).
Destroys the PDA cover model (ui_pda_destroy_cover_model), frees the PDA block with its heap (+0xa8) and clears the block pointer 0x09899de8. Side effects: heap, 0x09899de8. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Input of the PDA main menu (7 entries, 5 when restricted +0x298): increments the idle counter +0x10; cancel or square (0x8000) slides the PDA out (state 0xf, sound 0x7a58); confirm starts a 12-frame selection blink (byte +0xb4 bit 0, counter +0xb5, sound 0x7a05); up/down (repeat bits 0x10/0x40) move the cursor (low nibble of +0x0a, wrapping, sound 0x7a04). When the blink ends: entry 4 opens the confirmation prompt ui_pda_open_prompt_entry4, entry 5 ui_pda_open_prompt_entry5 (sound 0x7a0c), other entries switch the state to the u16 table 0x090fe6f0[entry]; the submenu cursor +0x0c is reset. Returns 0. Side effects: PDA block, sounds. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Input of the PDA three-entry submenu: cancel returns to the main menu reveal (state 2, sound 0x7a06); confirm starts the 12-frame selection blink (sound 0x7a05); up/down cycle the cursor +0x0c modulo 3, skipping entry 1 when +0x29c is 0 (sound 0x7a04). When the blink ends returns 3, 4 or 5 for entries 0, 1, 2; otherwise 0. Side effects: PDA block, sounds. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Input of the PDA five-entry submenu: cancel returns to the main menu reveal (state 2, sound 0x7a06); confirm starts the 12-frame selection blink (sound 0x7a05); up/down cycle the cursor +0x0c modulo 5 (sound 0x7a04). When the blink ends returns 6-10 for entries 0-4; otherwise 0. Side effects: PDA block, sounds. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Opens the confirmation prompt of PDA main-menu entry 5: clears the 0x120-byte list window record at PDA +0x168 and fills it (enabled, margins 10/10 and 8/0, font id 0xc, black text, field_strtbl entry 0x7e as text, PDA heap as allocator, cursor shown and cancel-to-button flags, button style 3, cancel button 3, selected button 2), opens it (ui_open_list_window), centres it on the 480 x 272 screen and sets the prompt byte +0x166 = 5. Side effects: PDA block. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step_main_menu).

Opens the confirmation prompt of PDA main-menu entry 4: same record as ui_pda_open_prompt_entry5 (PDA +0x168) but with max width 0x140, minimum size 0xf0 x 0x5a, field_strtbl entry 0x26 as text and selected button 3; opens and centres it and sets the prompt byte +0x166 = 4. Side effects: PDA block. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step_main_menu).
Returns the member pda_pack01.gim of archive (container_ehp_find_member), or NULL for a NULL archive. No side effects. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_open).

Returns the cached PDA cover model instance 0x09899e00, creating it on first use from archive: the model gx_pda_cover01.tms and its gx_pda_cover01.tmt; when the .tmt starts with the magic 'TGMT' (0x544d4754) it creates the instance (field_3d_create_model_instance(model, 0)) and attaches the animation (field_3d_set_animation), otherwise passes the .tmt (or NULL when missing) as the second creation argument. Returns NULL when nothing is cached and archive is NULL. Side effects: 0x09899e00, model instance. Callers: 3 (ui_pda_draw_cover_model, ui_pda_set_cover_anim_end, ui_pda_open).

Returns the cached member event_name.bin (0x09899e04), looking it up in archive on first use (container_ehp_find_member); NULL when not cached and archive is NULL. Side effects: 0x09899e04. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_open).

Returns the cached options string table (0x09899e08), on first use looking up option_msg_<c>.bin in archive with the language letter from the 6-byte table at 0x090fe748 indexed by save_get_language. Side effects: 0x09899e08. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_open).
Destroys the cached PDA cover model instance 0x09899e00 (field_3d_destroy_model_instance) and clears the pointer. Side effects: 0x09899e00. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_close).

column2: void * ui_field_draw_character_icon(void *list, uint character, int x, int y, int scale, int uv_offset, int crop, void *face_gim, void *body_gim)
column3: Draws a composed portrait icon for a generic character, scaled by scale percent with linear filtering: characters 0x79-0x8d and those whose character byte +0x09 is 5 use a fixed 0x33 x 0x54 cell of body_gim (texel origins hard-coded per id, e.g. 0x79 at (0x33, 0x54), 0x8a at (0, 0xfc)); others use world_get_character_model_ids: a 0x33 x 0x40 body cell of body_gim at u = id[1] * 0x33 drawn 16 * scale / 100 px lower, and a 0x33 x 0x32 face cell from image level (id[2] & 0xf) of face_gim at u = (id[0] % 10 % 5) * 0x33, v = (id[0] / 10) * 100 + (id[0] % 10 / 5) * 0x32. Argument 9 is on the stack. Returns the advanced display list (list unchanged when either GIM is missing or the character has no model ids). Side effects: display list. Callers: 1 (ui_field_call_draw_character_icon).

Opens the options screen: allocates a 0x3c-byte block from heap (pointer 0x09899e14), stores mode (+0x00), heap (+0x1c) and archive (+0x20), reads the current settings twice (working copy +0x08, original +0x10; ui_options_read_settings), sets the first item and cursor (+0x06/+0x04: 3 for mode 1, else 0) and three colours (+0x30/+0x34/+0x38: mode 2 0xffedecd5 / 0xff482b03 / 0xff482b03, mode 1 black, mode 0 white / black / white) and finds the skin texture named by entry mode of the 0x40-byte name table at 0x090fe764 (first name menu_opt01.gim) into +0x24. Side effects: heap, 0x09899e14. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Packs the current settings into an 8-byte options record: byte 0 bit 0 = save setting b0 bit 3, bits 1-2 = message speed (save_get_setting_b0_bits4_5), bits 3-4 = setting b1 bits 3-4, bits 5/6/7 = option flags 0/5/2; byte 1 bits 0-1 = setting b2 bits 1-2, bit 2 = option flag 4, bit 3 = option flag 3; u16 +2/+4/+6 = audio volume settings 2, 0 and 1 (audio_get_volume_setting). Side effects: writes settings. Callers: 1 (ui_options_open).

Writes an 8-byte options record back (the inverse of ui_options_read_settings): save setting b0 bit 3, message speed, the three volumes (audio_set_volume_setting 2, 0, 1), setting b1 bits 3-4, option flags 0, 5, 2, setting b2 bits 1-2 and option flags 4 and 3. Side effects: save settings, audio volumes. Callers: 1 (ui_options_step).
Frees the options block 0x09899e14 with the heap stored at its +0x1c. Side effects: heap. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).

Input of the options screen (block 0x09899e14, 12 items 0-11 on the working copy +0x08): confirm plays 0x7a05, applies the settings and returns 2; cancel plays 0x7a06, restores the original copy, applies it and returns 2. Up/down move the cursor +0x04 between the first item +0x06 and 11 (newly pressed at either end wraps), always skipping item 2 and, in mode 1, item 7. Left/right change the selected item: 0 and 6-8 and 11 are on/off bits (right clears, left sets; item 10 the reverse), 1 the message speed 0-2, 2-4 the volumes 0-15 of audio volume settings 2, 0, 1 (applied at once with audio_set_volume_setting; item 2 previews with sound 0x7a0a), 5 a 0-3 value, 9 a 0-2 value; each change plays 0x7a04. Increments the 24-bit frame counter +0x2c and sets the drawing flag +0x18. Returns 1 while open. Side effects: options block, audio volumes, save settings on exit, sounds. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_step).
Copies an 8-byte options settings record (four halfwords) from src to dst. Returns dst. Side effects: writes dst. Callers: 1 (ui_options_step).

Draws the options screen from the skin GIM (options block +0x24): the item groups (up to 4 sections whose item counts come from the halfword table 0x090fe894, mode 1 starting at section 2 with 7 items in the last), placed at x 0x6d (0x29 in mode 2) and y 0x22 (0x36 in mode 1, 0x17 in mode 2; +6 outside Japanese except mode 2); for each section a 0x107-wide frame box (colours 0x090fe824) and, for sections of more than one item, a header box and per-item frames (ui_options_draw_section_frame); then the cursor frame, every setting value (ui_options_draw_setting_value), every label and value text (ui_options_draw_item_label, ui_options_draw_item_value_text) and the help bar; clears the drawing flag +0x18. No return value (list lost in the decompilation). Side effects: display list, font state. Callers: 1 (ui_pda_draw_screen).

column3: Draws the options cursor: converts the cursor item (+0x04; items 2-4, 5-11 belong to sections 2 and 3, mode 1 skips item 7) into a row y by adding 0xe per multi-item section header and 10 per section gap before it plus 0xc per row (minus the first item), and draws a 0xfa-wide highlight frame there (ui_options_draw_highlight_frame(list, x, y, 0, 0)).
